study_material.title: Direction Sense Test - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Direction problems track a walker through turns and distances, then ask the final direction or straight-line distance from the start. Draw the path on a quick N-E-S-W grid and apply Pythagoras at the end.
learning_objectives: Convert left/right turns into compass directions

concepts.heading: 1. The Compass Frame
concepts.body: North up, East right, South down, West left. Every solution starts with a small sketch: mark the start, draw each leg to rough scale, label the end. Never solve directions in your head.

concepts.heading: 2. Turns
concepts.body: Facing North: right = East, left = West. Facing East: right = South, left = North. A 'right turn' is always 90 degrees clockwise, 'left' anticlockwise. About turn = 180 degrees. Track the CURRENT facing after every turn.

concepts.heading: 3. Net Displacement
concepts.body: Sum the north-south legs and the east-west legs separately (opposite directions cancel). The shortest distance = sqrt(NS^2 + EW^2). Walking 3 km north then 4 km east ends 5 km from the start (3-4-5 triple).

concepts.heading: 4. Shadows
concepts.body: The sun rises in the east: morning shadows point WEST; evening shadows point EAST. At noon shadows point north (in India, northern hemisphere). If a person's shadow falls to their right in the morning, they face south.

formulas: Morning shadow west, evening shadow east
shortcut_methods: Cancel opposite legs before applying Pythagoras
Look for 3-4-5 and 5-12-13 triples in the leg lengths
Rotate the whole page mentally when facing changes confuse you - or just re-sketch
common_mistakes: Losing the current facing after multiple turns
Adding all distances instead of netting opposite directions
Reversing morning and evening shadow directions
study_material.summary: Sketch, track facing after each turn, net the legs, Pythagoras for distance, and remember: morning shadows point west.

solved_examples.question: A man walks 3 km north, then 4 km east. How far is he from the start?
Facing north, a man turns right, then right again. Which direction does he face?
A man walks 10 m south, 10 m east, then 10 m north. Where is he relative to the start?
solved_examples.step_by_step: South and north legs cancel; only 10 m east remains.

solved_examples.question: One morning, Ravi's shadow falls exactly to his right. Which direction is he facing?
solved_examples.step_by_step: Morning shadow points west. West on his right means he faces south.

practice_questions.question: Facing east, you turn left. You now face:

Facing south-west, an about turn leaves you facing:
A walks 5 km north, 3 km east, 5 km south. How far and in which direction from the start?
practice_questions.explanation: North and south cancel; 3 km east remains.

practice_questions.question: Facing north, you turn right, then left, then right. You now face:
In the evening, Meera's shadow falls to her left. She is facing:
practice_questions.explanation: Evening shadow points east; east on her left means she faces south.

practice_questions.question: From home, Ria cycles 4 km east, 3 km south, 4 km west and 7 km north. Where is she now?
A man facing west turns 135 degrees clockwise. He now faces:
practice_questions.explanation: West + 135 clockwise: W -> NW (45) -> N (90) -> NE (135).

topic_test.title: Direction Sense Test - Topic Test
instructions: +1 for correct, -0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
Sketch every path; never track directions purely mentally.

questions.explanation: Sun rises in the east; back to it means facing west.

questions.question: C walks 20 m north, turns right and walks 30 m, turns right and walks 35 m, turns left and walks 15 m. Net east-west displacement:
questions.explanation: East legs: 30 + 15 = 45 m east (the 20 N and 35 S legs affect only NS).

questions.question: From P, walk 10 km south to Q, then 10 km east to R, then 10 km north to S. The distance PS is:
questions.explanation: NS cancels: S is 10 km due east of P.
